device.whisperCpp: 1.9.5-dev (482279b), built for arm64, run from adb shell, 4 threads

testSet.note: No owner voice. Commands are synthetic (Piper en_US-lessac, en_GB-alan). Raw audio and per-clip transcripts kept off Git.

method.whisper: whisper-cli per clip, fresh process (model load included), wall clock from /proc/uptime at 10 ms resolution. small.en run was interrupted by a USB disconnect and resumed; 20 clips in each half.
method.android: Test app trace.a8.stt feeds the WAV to SpeechRecognizer through EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE at real time, plus 0.5 s silence; one app launch per clip, 2 s gap. Time is from startListening to onResults, so it includes the clip length. Single-utterance session (EXTRA_SEGMENTED_SESSION false).
method.wer: score.py: lowercase, punctuation stripped, numbers matched as spoken or digit by digit, British spellings folded.
method.permission: Without RECORD_AUDIO the on-device recognizer still worked; the default recognizer returned ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS (9) on every clip. RECORD_AUDIO was granted to the test app with owner approval; the microphone was never opened by the app.

findings.fileInputAccepted: Android 17 accepts audio from a file descriptor (EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE) for both on-device and default recognizers.
findings.offlineFlagUsesOnDeviceModel: default + EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE matched on-device transcripts word for word on 26 of 27 clips; default without the flag matched only 20 of 39.
findings.longUtterancesCut: Android routes stop at the first pause in single-utterance mode: 4 (on-device), 4 (default), 8 (default+offline) LibriSpeech clips returned under 70% of the reference words. This drives their LibriSpeech WER, not word accuracy.
findings.onDeviceReliability: on-device API (createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer) failed 13 of 40 clips with ERROR_CLIENT (5) or NO_MATCH (7) even with one launch per clip; default+offline failed 1 of 40.
